text: They arrived at the other side of the lake, in the region of the Gerasenes.
As soon as Jesus stepped out of the boat, a man with an unclean spirit came out from among the tombs to meet him.
The man lived among the tombs, and no one could restrain him anymore, not even with a chain,
because he had often been bound with shackles and chains, but he would snap the chains and break the shackles apart — no one had the strength to control him.
Night and day, among the tombs and on the hillsides, he kept crying out and cutting himself with stones.
When he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and fell on his knees before him,
shouting at the top of his voice, What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you in God's name, don't torment me!
(Jesus had already been telling him, Come out of this man, you unclean spirit!)
Jesus asked him, What's your name? My name is Legion, he answered, because there are many of us.
And he begged Jesus repeatedly not to send them out of that region.
Now there was a large herd of pigs feeding on the hillside nearby.
The demons begged him, Send us into the pigs, so we can enter them.
He gave them permission, and the unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs; the herd, about two thousand of them, rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned.
Those tending the pigs ran off and spread the news in the town and countryside, and people came out to see what had happened.
When they reached Jesus, they saw the man who had been possessed by the legion of demons sitting there, clothed and thinking clearly, and they were afraid.
Those who had witnessed it told the others what had happened to the demon-possessed man, and about the pigs as well.
Then the people began pleading with Jesus to leave their region.
As he was getting into the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed begged to go with him.
Jesus would not let him, but told him instead, Go home to your own people and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and how he has had mercy on you.
So the man went away and began proclaiming in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him, and everyone was amazed.
When Jesus had crossed again by boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered around him while he was still by the lake.
Then one of the synagogue rulers, a man named Jairus, came up, and seeing Jesus, fell at his feet,
pleading urgently with him, My little daughter is dying. Please come and lay your hands on her so she'll be healed and live.
So Jesus went with him. A large crowd followed, pressing in around him.
Among them was a woman who had been suffering from a flow of blood for twelve years.
She had endured a great deal under many doctors and had spent all she had, yet instead of improving she had grown worse.
Having heard about Jesus, she came up through the crowd behind him and touched his cloak,
because she had told herself, If I can just touch his clothes, I will be healed.
At once the bleeding stopped, and she felt in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
At the same moment Jesus, aware that power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd and asked, Who touched my clothes?
His disciples said to him, You see the crowd pressing in on you, and yet you ask who touched you?
But he kept looking around to see who had done it.
Then the woman, trembling with fear because she knew what had happened to her, came and fell down before him and told him the whole truth.
He said to her, Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace and be freed from your suffering.
While he was still speaking, some people came from the synagogue ruler's house and said, Your daughter has died. Why bother the teacher any more?
Overhearing what was said, Jesus told the synagogue ruler, Don't be afraid; just believe.
He did not let anyone follow him except Peter, James, and John, James's brother.
They came to the house, and Jesus saw a commotion, with people weeping and wailing loudly.
He went in and said to them, Why all this commotion and weeping? The child is not dead, but asleep.
They laughed at him. But he put them all outside, and taking the child's father and mother and his own companions, he went in to where the child was.
Taking her by the hand, he said to her, Talitha koum!, which means, Little girl, I say to you, get up.
Immediately the girl stood up and began to walk around (she was twelve years old). At this everyone was utterly astonished.
He gave them strict orders that no one should know about this, and told them to give her something to eat.
